references.citation: Bickel, P. J., Hammel, E. A., O'Connell, J. W. (1975). Sex bias in graduate admissions: Data from Berkeley. Science 187(4175), 398-404.

target.task: Our university tried two ways of teaching first-year calculus in 2026: method A (flipped classroom) and method B (traditional lectures). Sections differ a lot in how hard their students find the course. Each row of the data is a tuple (section, method, passed, enrolled). Write a Python function better_method(rows) that returns "A" or "B" for the method with better results, or "tie" when neither is better.

rules.text: Rows may come in any order.
If both methods have identical pass counts and enrolment in every section, return tie.
When one method has the higher pass rate in every section and overall, return that method.

target.format: Reply with one Python code block that contains only the function and any helpers it needs.

shared_surface_features.feature: comparing pass rates of two groups

relation: Compare groups within each stratum before pooling, because pooling can reverse the answer.

notes: Only unambiguous data are tested: in the reversal data every section favours B while the pooled rate favours A. What to return when sections disagree is left open, so a Mantel-Haenszel answer and a 'tie when mixed' answer both pass. The phrase 'better results' in the target leaves pooled vs stratified open; that is deliberate so the role decides.
